title: Elliptic Curve Cryptography
subtitle: ECDSA, ECDH, and why ECC beats RSA for size

content.text: ECC provides the same security as RSA with much smaller key sizes. A 256-bit ECC key is as strong as a 3072-bit RSA key.

content.code:
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import ec
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import hashes

# Generate ECDSA key pair (P-256 / secp256r1)
private_key = ec.generate_private_key(ec.SECP256R1())
public_key = private_key.public_key()

# Sign
signature = private_key.sign(b"document", ec.ECDSA(hashes.SHA256()))

# Verify
public_key.verify(signature, b"document", ec.ECDSA(hashes.SHA256()))
print("ECDSA signature valid")

# ECDH key exchange
other_private = ec.generate_private_key(ec.SECP256R1())
shared_key = private_key.exchange(ec.ECDH(), other_private.public_key())
print(len(shared_key), "bytes shared secret")

content.text: Use P-256 (secp256r1) or X25519 for new applications. Avoid P-192.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of ECC over RSA?
options: ECC provides equivalent security with much smaller key sizes
questions.explanation: ECC achieves the same security level as RSA with dramatically smaller keys, reducing computation and bandwidth.

faq.a: A modern elliptic curve designed by Bernstein for high security and performance. Used in TLS 1.3, SSH, and Signal Protocol.
